hints: Look closely at the word all. Remember, some viruses store their genes as DNA and others store them as RNA, never both in the same virus.
Now sort the four chemicals into DNA-only, RNA-only, or found in both types of nucleic acid. Which one is shared?
walkthrough:
**Recall what a virus must carry**

Every virus must carry nucleic acid to make new viruses, but it is either DNA or RNA. Think of it as a choice, DNA viruses like adenovirus, or RNA viruses like influenza and coronavirus.

**Sort the bases and sugars**

DNA uses the bases adenine, thymine, cytosine, guanine and the sugar deoxyribose. RNA uses adenine, uracil, cytosine, guanine and the sugar ribose. Notice that cytosine and guanine are the common ones.

**Pick what must be in both**

Uracil, ribose and thymine are only in one type, so they cannot be in all viruses. Guanine is in both DNA and RNA, so every virus must contain it.

options.A: Uracil replaces thymine only in RNA, so DNA viruses do not contain it.
options.B: Ribose is the pentose sugar of RNA only. DNA viruses use deoxyribose instead.
options.C: Thymine is found only in DNA, so RNA viruses do not contain it.
options.D: Guanine is a purine base found in both DNA and RNA, so whether a virus is a DNA virus or an RNA virus, it will contain guanine.
